title: Machine learning on plasma metabolites predicts acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery
summary: In 214 individuals (122 with acute kidney injury, 92 controls), untargeted and targeted metabolomics with several machine learning algorithms identified plasma metabolites associated with cardiac surgery-associated AKI; gluconic acid, fumaric acid and pseudouridine were upregulated. A random forest with clinical parameters and metabolites reached an AUC of 0.939 (95% CI 0.879-0.998), and the three metabolites rose over time in a swine AKI model. The abstract states a validation cohort confirmed the model, but its figure was truncated; the cohort is small.
ai_technology: Random forest and other machine learning algorithms on plasma metabolomics and clinical parameters
organization: Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College

evidence.tested: Discovery in 214 patients, a swine AKI model for time-dependent metabolite changes (ancillary), and a separate validation cohort.
evidence.unknown: Validation-cohort performance figure was not visible in the abstract text; generalization beyond a small cohort; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Selects discriminating metabolites and combines them with clinical parameters in a random forest classifier.
